subject: Chemistry
title: Pasteurization: Heat That Saves Lives
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Pasteurization: Heat That Saves Lives.

hook.text: Louis Pasteur proved that heating liquids kills bacteria. His technique saves millions of lives every year.

buildup.text: Before pasteurization, milk carried tuberculosis, typhoid, and diphtheria. Thousands of children died annually.

discovery.text: Heating milk to 72°C for 15 seconds kills 99.999% of harmful bacteria while preserving taste and nutrition.

twist.text: Ultra-high temperature (UHT) treatment at 135°C for 2 seconds makes milk shelf-stable for 6 months—no refrigeration.

climax.text: Pasteur's process also saved the French wine and beer industries from spoilage—that was his original goal.

punchline.text: Brief heat, dead bacteria, safe milk. Simple chemistry, millions of lives saved.

quiz.question: What temperature and time does standard pasteurization use?
options: 50°C for 30 minutes—slow heating preserves more nutrients

details.summary: Pasteurization uses precisely controlled heat to kill pathogenic bacteria in food without destroying nutritional value or flavor. Louis Pasteur developed the process in the 1860s after proving that microorganisms, not spontaneous generation, caused food spoilage and fermentation.
details.whyItMatters: Pasteurization is one of the most important public health interventions in history. It eliminated deadly milk-borne diseases that killed thousands of children annually and extended the shelf life of dairy worldwide.
takeaways: Heat denatures bacterial proteins and enzymes at specific temperatures
Standard milk pasteurization uses 72°C for 15 seconds to kill pathogens
Pasteur's germ theory overturned the ancient idea of spontaneous generation

faq.question: Does pasteurization destroy the nutritional value of milk?
faq.answer: Pasteurization causes minimal nutritional loss. Heat-sensitive vitamin C decreases slightly, but milk is not a significant vitamin C source. Proteins, calcium, and other key nutrients remain largely unaffected. The food safety benefits far outweigh any minor nutritional changes.

faq.question: What is the difference between pasteurization and sterilization?
faq.answer: Pasteurization kills pathogenic bacteria but not all microorganisms, allowing natural flavor and requiring refrigerated storage. Sterilization, as in UHT processing at 135°C for seconds, kills virtually all microbes, enabling room-temperature storage for months but slightly altering taste.
